alex: quick heads up — during nightly shadow runs we saw a small but consistent quality blip for FP8 on a subset of long-tail prompt families (legal / code-mix). posting examples and a summary. https://internal/shadow/8076543 :eyes:
priya: thanks. i sketched an initial diff in the eval harness — KL/bleu drift starts ~token 180 and amplifies after kv-cache eviction events. short logs below.
priya: ```
# sample from harness: prompt family id=ll-code-013
post-quant kl: 0.32 -> 0.67 after token 210
fluency: 0.98 -> 0.94
metric_delta window=64 tokens
```
sam_runtime: interesting — runtime telemetry shows bursty cache_evictions around the same timeframe (evictions/sec spikes from 2 -> 18). looks correlated with our small-kv-gc heuristic under mixed workloads.
alex: are we confident this is eviction triggering FP8 numerical instability vs FP8 itself being brittle on those ops?
priya: we ran offline where we prevented eviction and degradation disappeared. so likely eviction + re-quant path interaction.
jordan_ops: can we tag requests so we can filter production traces by "quant_eviction_recompute"? current traces only show "kv_eviction" and a generic "recompute" tag.
sam_runtime: yeah we can add a per-request annotation: quant_path_change=[none|fp8->int8|fp8->4bit], and quant_fallback_reason=[eviction|overtemp|latency_slo|quality_alert]. low overhead.
eval-bot: shadow-eval run 8076543200 summary: fp8 baseline qdrop=1.8% on affected families, fp8->int8 fallback qdrop=0.4%, fp8->4bit qdrop=2.9%. recommended intermediate fallback to int8 for transient evictions.
priya: proposal: when we detect a cache-eviction followed by recompute within 500ms, do an immediate local score check (cheap n=4 sampling) and if KL > 0.1 or perplexity up by > 3% switch path fp8->int8 for that request. fall back to fp8 after warm run of 5 requests.
alex: that heuristic seems reasonable but we need to avoid oscillation — what if eviction keeps happening? add hysteresis like backoff doubling.
sam_runtime: agree. sketching a small state machine:
```
state: FP8
on eviction_recompute -> quick_sample -> if bad -> switch INT8, counter=1
on subsequent eviction within 30s -> counter++ , if counter >=3 -> degrade to INT8 for 60s (circuit)
after stable run (no evictions for 60s && counter < 1) -> try FP8 warmup (1 sampled request)
```
priya: also recommend tagging telemetry with sample_estimates so we can compute precision-specific moving averages. i can add fields e.g. sample_kl, sample_ppl to the ingest schema.
jordan_ops: ops + SRE OK with exposing these extra tags? storage cost concerns?
alex: keep sampling rare (1 in 200 by default) and only turn on denser sampling for affected endpoints. store aggregated rollups per-minute instead of per-request when dense.
priya: also we should capture the exact model-quant variant id in traces (e.g., model:v1::fp8-a1) so we can map regressions to profile versions.
sam_runtime: note: switching precision mid-request requires kernel compatibility. for some model shims we need to rebind kernels which adds ~15ms; that's acceptable for quality fallbacks but not great for latency SLOs. need to gate by route latency tier.
alex: ops tradeoff: quality vs latency. for latency-sensitive routes we'd prefer graceful degrade to smaller token window (truncate) or route to dedicated INT8 lane rather than rebind mid-request.
jordan_ops: +1. we should add a route-level config: quant_fallback_policy = [no-mid-request-rebind | allow-rebind-force-int8 | prefer-routing]. configurable per-customer.
priya: action items: 1) add per-request quant annotations (sam) 2) add cheap sampling check + sample fields in eval ingest (priya) 3) implement state machine + hysteresis in runtime (sam) 4) ops config knob for route-level policy + storage rollups (jordan)
alex: timeline?
sam_runtime: can push telemetry + annotations in 3 days, state machine PoC in a week.
jordan_ops: policy knobs and storage limits config i'll do in parallel, ETA 1 week.
priya: i'll add eval harness tests and shadow config for targeted families, can be ready in 5 days.
alex: cool. can we also create a small canary that enables the full fallback for one non-critical endpoint next Wednesday? :thumbsup:
jordan_ops: scheduling canary for Wed 10:00 PT. i'll post the runbook.
priya: will prepare prompt sets and expected deltas.
eval-bot: scheduled shadow session for canary id=canary-8076 on 8076543600.
alex: thanks all — we'll monitor the new telemetry closely and reconvene after canary. :rocket:
